'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war]]
***The [[United Nations]] suspends [[humanitarian aid]] delivery at the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]]-constructed [[Gaza floating pier]] pending investigations on whether the pier was used in the [[Israel]]i [[2024 Nuseirat rescue operation|raid on]] the [[Nuseirat refugee camp]] and on the security of humanitarian workers at the pier. [https://apnews.com/article/pier-humanitarian-aid-gaza-israel-un-2465291ca9308f9d97e3cc51a8cab6c7 (AP)]
***The [[United States]] military plans to temporarily dismantle the Gaza floating pier and move it to [[Israel]] following predictions of rough seas, suspending humanitarian aid shipments at the pier for the third time in the past month. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/us-humanitarian-aid-pier-off-gaza-become-inoperable/story?id=111058739 (ABC News)]
***The [[United States State Department]] officially adds the Israeli group [[Tsav 9]] to its list of [[United States sanctions#Targeted parties|sanctioned entities]] for impeding the delivery of [[humanitarian aid]] to the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8vvlz063e2o (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-impose-sanctions-israeli-group-that-attacked-gaza-aid-2024-06-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Germany]] vetoes a [[European Union]] sanction package that would prevent EU members from re-exporting Russian [[Liquefied natural gas|liquefied natural gas]] from EU ports and prevent EU companies from selling sanctioned products to [[Russia]]. [https://kyivindependent.com/germany-blocks-sanctions-on-russian-gas/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')]
**[[Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] announces that he is ready for a [[ceasefire]] if [[Ukraine]] withdraws from [[Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine|Russian-claimed territories]], including liberated areas, and stops its [[Ukraine–NATO relations|accession to NATO]]. However, Ukraine rejects the offer. [https://apnews.com/article/putin-russia-ukraine-war-4f58423548b3d2e8594c9d9eb8e9d36e (AP)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of El Fasher]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] kill [[Ali Yagoub Gibril|Ali Yaqoub Gibril]], a commander of the [[Rapid Support Forces]] in [[Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article286999/ (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**The [[United States military]] launches attacks on and destroys seven [[Houthi]] radar stations in [[Yemen]] in retaliation after a merchant sailor went missing following Houthi strikes on ships in the [[Red Sea]]. [https://www.seattletimes.com/business/us-military-targets-houthi-radar-sites-in-yemen-after-a-merchant-sailor-goes-missing/ (''The Seattle Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least six people are killed and more than 1,000 tourists are stranded in heavy rains and landslides across the state of [[Sikkim]], [[India]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/heavy-rain-landslides-kill-6-indias-sikkim-2000-tourists-stranded-2024-06-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 misinformation by governments]]
**[[Reuters]] releases a report that alleges that the United States military conducted a clandestine online campaign, ordered by the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] in 2020 and ended by the [[Biden administration]] in 2021, to discredit the [[CoronaVac]] vaccine of China-based manufacturer [[Sinovac Biotech]] in the [[Philippines]] and other developing countries. [https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/usa-covid-propaganda/ (Reuters)]
*The [[World Health Organization]] officially confirms a human [[Influenza A virus subtype H9N2]] case in a child in [[West Bengal|West Bengal state]], [[India]]. [https://www.businessinsider.in/science/health/news/who-confirms-human-case-of-bird-flu-in-india-h9n2-virus-detected-in-a-four-year-child-in-west-bengal/articleshow/110941217.cms (''Business Insider'')]
*The [[Netherlands]]-flagged dredger ''Vox Maxima'' collides with the stationary bunker vessel ''Marine Honour'' in [[Pasir Panjang#Pasir Panjang Terminal|Pasir Panjang Terminal]], [[Singapore]], causing an [[oil spill]] that spreads across several [[Southern Islands]] alongside the beaches in [[East Coast Park]]. [[Sentosa]] announce a temporary suspension of any water activities while their beaches remain open. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/oil-spill-reaches-s-pore-s-southern-islands-sparking-concerns-over-corals-weakened-from-bleaching (''Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Nigerien crisis (2023–2024)|Nigerien crisis]]
**The [[Judiciary of Niger|Niger State Security Court]] retracts the immunity of deposed [[List of heads of state of Niger|president]] [[Mohamed Bazoum]], thereby allowing Bazoum to be prosecuted for [[high treason]] and undermining [[national security]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/14/niger-court-scraps-immunity-of-deposed-president-bazoum (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Kyrgyzstan]] arrests 15 alleged [[Islamic State – Khorasan Province]] supporters in [[Bishkek]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2024/06/14/kyrgyzstan-arrests-15-alleged-isis-supporters (Al Arabiya)]
*The [[United States Department of State]] designates the [[far-right]] [[Nordic Resistance Movement]] as a terrorist organization. Three of its leaders are subsequently designated as [[Specially Designated Global Terrorist]]s. [https://edition.cnn.com/2024/06/14/politics/us-designates-nordic-neo-nazi-group-terrorists/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[Cambodian National Police]] and the National Authority to Combat Drugs seize and destroy seven tons of [[illicit drugs]], mostly [[methamphetamine]], worth US$70 million as part of a crackdown operation. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/cambodian-authorities-burn-70m-seized-illegal-drugs-major-crackdown (Fox News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 South African general election]]
**[[Cyril Ramaphosa]] is re-elected as [[President of South Africa]] for a second term. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/south-africas-national-assembly-re-elects-cyril-ramaphosa-president-2024-06-14/ (Reuters)]
